chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Friday prayer is obligatory upon the one who is within two Farsakhs of it.

key_terms.فَرْسَخَيْنِ: Two Farsakhs (a unit of distance, approx. 6 miles)

ai.seo_question: What is the distance limit for the obligation of Friday prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the geographical scope of the Friday prayer's obligation, defining the radius as two Farsakhs (roughly six miles) from the prayer venue. In Shia jurisprudence, this distance criterion helps determine who is exempt from the communal Friday prayer in favor of the individual Dhuhr prayer, reflecting the practical considerations of early Islamic community organization. The ruling underscores the balance between communal unity and individual ease in religious duties.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim and Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Friday (Salāt) is Obligatory upon the one who was upon two Farsakhs (6 miles) from it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah who have said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Friday Salah (prayer) is not obligatory upon those who are two farsakh (about six miles) away (from the location of the congregation).”’
